AlternateTargets: register and take a monastic place
take an assigned place in the monks’ hall
SearchAliases: receive a place in the monks' hall
Senses.Explanation: To register for residence and receive an assigned place in a monastery. The Chan Monastic Regulations gives the procedure: a new arrival waits a day or two, presents himself at the hall office with his ordination document, and requests residence. After registration he stores his luggage, hangs his bowl, and arranges his bedding in the unnamed monks' hall. The Imperially Revised Baizhang Monastic Code states the order more compactly: one seeking residence first presents himself at the guest office, then registers at the hall office, after which his assigned place is settled. When the abbot permits registration, the attendant's office notifies the hall office; tea and the bed register follow, and the newcomer enters the common quarters. Encounter narratives use the same institutional verb. Yexian Guixing tells Fushan Fayuan and Tianyi Yihuai, 'You two want to investigate Zen; go register' (你兩箇要參禪，却去掛搭). Fayun Faxiu directs that Ziqing register elsewhere until a place becomes vacant and he can enter the hall (且令別處掛搭，候此間單位空，即令入堂). These sources make the concrete Zen bend visible: registration is not generic lodging but formal admission into the monastery's offices, hall, bed register, and common quarters.
Senses.Note: The headword occurs 145 times in 38 allowlisted texts. The regulations distinguish seeking registration, the abbot permitting it, new registrants, greater and lesser registration procedures, returning to the hall, tea for new registrants, and thanks after registration. “Seek registration” occurs 8 times in 4 texts; “permit registration” occurs twice in two. The corpus therefore supplies a concrete lodging-and-admission procedure. In some biographies the completed verb simply marks that a traveler resided at the named monastery.
